title: Ring tool anchor order: keep the user's ring order, insert by least added surface length, never self-cross
description:
User report 2026-10-03 on the crawfish tail (fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl, ring_03, 12+ authored anchors along a long thin boundary): the ring crosses itself depending on the order anchors are clicked; clicking carefully in the right order avoids it, and the order the tool picks ignores what surface (geodesic) distance between anchors would say. A ring must never cross itself.

Current mechanism (read before changing): every edit (RingTool.addAuthoredAnchor, deleteSelectedAnchor, drags) re-runs AuthoredSplineRing.trace on the whole authored list. trace fits one plane through all anchors (fitPlane, leaning on the draft's base normal by BASE_NORMAL_PULL_OF_SPREAD), walks the plane's loop starting at the FIRST anchor's crossing, matches each anchor to its nearest loop point by straight-line 3D distance (AuthoredSplineRing.trace lines ~129-141), and SplineAnchorFit.accept/insertionSlot sorts anchors by that loop index; supporting anchors are then placed on the plane loop. Click order leaks in through (a) ties: anchors mapping to the same loop point keep insertion order ('an authored one goes after those at its point'); (b) the first anchor choosing which loop of a multi-loop plane cut is walked; (c) a failing add being reverted. On a non-planar boundary of a thin part, many anchors sit far off the plane loop and their nearest loop points are weak, tied, or on the opposite side of the part (close in 3D, far along the surface), so the order is effectively decided by click order, and a wrong one traces a figure-eight. The supporting anchors on the plane loop also make the curve zigzag out to each authored anchor and back (user screenshot).

Step 1, confirm the cause before fixing: take ring_03's anchors from fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl (on a tmp copy), trace them in many permutations with the same first anchor and with different first anchors; record which orders self-cross, and whether every crossing order involves tied or near-tied loop matches or a different walked loop. Put the table on the ticket. If the data disagrees with the hypothesis, report that instead of building the fix below.

Fix (expected): the anchor cycle becomes ring state, not something re-derived. The plane is only for starting a ring (the first one to three anchors, and the hover preview). Once a draft has a cycle, a new authored anchor is inserted between the neighbours where it adds the least surface length (cheapest insertion with geodesic distances from SurfaceGeodesics, never straight-line), and existing anchors keep their order; drags keep order. The spline through a ring with enough authored anchors runs through them with only the supporting anchors it needs between consecutive authored ones (fit per span against the geodesic between them, not against a global plane loop). Invariant: a draft or confirmed ring is a simple closed curve on the surface. An insertion or drag that would make it cross itself tries the other candidate slots in increasing added length and is refused with a status message if none is simple. Saved rings keep loading: spline_ring's points list is already in ring order, so reading it back must take that order as the cycle (check how spline_ring/adoptGraphRings rebuild rings and keep them stable). Clean design; no special case for thin parts.
definition-of-done: 1. The permutation experiment on ring_03 is on the ticket and names the confirmed cause. 2. Adding anchors to an existing draft in any order gives the same ring when the anchors are the same set added around the ring, and the order is the cheapest-insertion order by surface length; existing anchors never reorder. 3. No edit can produce a self-crossing ring: a crossing edit is refused with a message. 4. With many authored anchors the spline passes through them without zigzagging back to a plane loop. 5. fixtures/fertility_rings.dsl's 13 ring fingerprints and fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl's 12 rings reload unchanged (load read-only, never save over either); if a ring's shape must change, say which and why. 6. Unit tests: a thin-strip surface where anchors on the two long edges are closer in 3D across the strip than along it, added in shuffled orders, never self-crosses and gives the same cycle; a crossing edit is refused.
testing-plan: 1. Permutation experiment on a tmp copy of crawfish_rings.dsl (ring_03), table on the ticket. 2. Unit tests above. 3. Live: in the ring-tool scene on a tmp copy, redraw the tail ring by clicking anchors in a deliberately bad order; screenshot before (master) and after under tmp/. 4. Fertility and crawfish ring reload checks.

Ring order is in saved indices.

No add failed and was reverted in any click run.
ring_04 (7 anchors) for contrast: the plane cuts an 8-crossing stray loop and 5 of 7 anchors tie on it; the saved (user-clicked) order is simple, but all 6 shuffles keeping the first anchor give other orders that cross (1-4 crossings), and 5 of 6 other first anchors cross or fail to snap. ring_00 and ring_06 (fat sections, no ties, anchors 6-13 edges off the loop): every order identical and simple.
CONFIRMED CAUSE: the order is not a property of the ring; it is re-derived on every edit by projecting anchors onto the plane loop. (b) dominates on ring_03: the plane is the same for every order, but the walked loop starts at the first anchor's crossing, so the first anchor alone decides the loop (11 different loops/orders from 12 first anchors; whole-list shuffles behind a fixed first anchor are bit-identical, and the tool keeps the first click first, so "click order matters" means "which anchor you click first"). (a) ties decide the rest when the walked loop is a stray small component (ring_04, ring_03 first 12). (c) reverted adds: not observed. Separately, anchors sit 29-78 mean edges off the plane loop, so even the saved ring_03 order re-traces with 4 crossings (its snapped loop is not a simple cycle today): the supporting anchors on the plane loop pull the spline out to each anchor and back, and those zigzags cross (first crossings 1-38 edges from an anchor).

Fix built (worktree craw-44, uncommitted). The anchor cycle is ring state: AuthoredSplineRing.trace takes anchors in ring order; up to PLANE_STARTED_ANCHORS (3) the fitted plane's loop shapes the ring as before (order of <=3 is unique), past that the given order is kept and each span's reference is the geodesic to the next anchor (geodesicCycleReference), so supporting anchors sit between their own two anchors and the spline no longer zigzags back to a plane loop. Where geodesics would make the ring cross itself or double back at an anchor (anchors leaving part of the girdle uncovered, e.g. crawfish ring_06), the plane loop is used instead provided it keeps the anchors' order. New anchors: AuthoredSplineRing.insert / slotsByAddedLength price each slot by the surface detour from that span of the ring out to the click (cheapest insertion into the ring's own path, SurfaceGeodesics.distanceToLabels, edge-path Dijkstra), try slots cheapest first and refuse with "no place for the anchor keeps the ring simple: the ring would cross itself near x,y,z" when none keeps a simple ring simple. Drags (RingTool.moveSelectedAnchor), deletes and confirm refuse an edit that would make a simple draft cross itself. New SurfacePathCrossings (crossing spans inside a shared face, revisited vertices, zero-width retraces cancelled) is the simplicity test. SplineAnchorFit now measures deviation two-sided and per segment (reference stretch between the segment's own anchors), so a spline that cuts across a thin part is caught. SplineRingNode/saved rings load with the saved order as the cycle.
Tests: unit RingAnchorOrderTest (stadium tube 0.12 thick, anchors 0.18-0.2 apart on each face: 12 shuffled click orders give one simple cycle, existing anchors never reorder; a crossing drag on a round tube is refused); mvn test 421/421; benchmark RingAnchorOrderBenchmark (#traceShuffledAnchorOrders, #fingerprintEverySplineRing). On ring_03, 7 simulated click orders (saved base normal, refused clicks retried): 6 give the same simple cycle 0 3 5 4 2 1 12 7 6 9 10 8 11 (2 needed one re-click); the 7th (first clicks 0,9,12) ends on another simple-or-not ring with clicks refused. That cycle DISAGREES with the saved ring_03 order 0..12, which crosses itself (4 crossings) on master and still does: saved rings load in their saved order, so ring_03 needs redrawing.
Fingerprints (read-only reload of tmp copies): unchanged fertility 07 08 09 10 13 14 16 17, crawfish 00 01 09 12. Changed: fertility 05 06 11 12 15 (1.2-1.8 mean edges; supporting anchors now fit to geodesic spans, no plane-loop zigzag), crawfish 04 05 07 11 (1.5-5 edges, same reason), crawfish 08 10 (1-anchor rings, 0.5-1.3 edges: the two-sided fit adds one support where master's spline skipped a stretch of its loop), crawfish 06 (20 edges: plane fallback kept, but master's ring was 19% shorter than its own plane loop, cutting across it; now follows it), crawfish 03 (crossing before and after; saved order).
Live: ring-tool on tmp copy without ring_03, same bad click order 0,7,5,6,4,9,2,10,1,8,12,11,3: master takes all 13 and draws a tangle of strands into the notch (tmp/craw44/master-back.png); after takes 9, refuses 9,10,8,3 with the crossing message, draft simple (tmp/craw44/after-back.png).

User's crawfish segmentation (82 spline_ring rings; ring_00..ring_12 kept, ring_01/03/06 edited, 70 new, saved 2026-10-04 via the CRAW-44 F5 entry into tmp/craw44/crawfish_rings_f5.dsl) promoted to the tracked fixture ixdar-app/src/main/resources/dsl/fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl (md5 28252ee7...). It lands with CRAW-44; master's 'Ring Tool (crawfish)' launch entry opens it.
